chunks: It is He who enables you to travel over land and sea. When you sail in ships in a favourable breeze, you rejoice. But when a gale begins to blow and the waves dash against them from every side they realise that they have been caught in it, (and) they call on God in all faith: "If You save us from this we shall ever be grateful."

key_terms.مُخْلِصِينَ لَهُ الدِّينَ: Making religion sincere for Him (sincere devotion)

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about human gratitude during times of hardship and travel?
ai.summary: This verse from Surah Yunus (10:22) illustrates the human condition of *ghaflah* (heedlessness) during times of ease, where divine facilitation is taken for granted until a sudden trial, such as a storm, forces sincere supplication (*dua*). Shia scholars often highlight this as a paradigm for spiritual awakening, where adversity strips away ego and compels the believer to return to God with pure devotion (*ikhlas*). The narrative serves as a reminder that gratitude (*shukr*) is most profound when earned through the recognition of divine mercy in the midst of chaos.
